## Errors and environment

Ramabana reports a failure in one of two ways. `AgentError` is a
refusal: something the harness will not do, with a message the user can
act on, such as a write outside the open folders or a model whose key is
missing. It is shalya’s `HostError` under another name, so a refusal
from a tool and a refusal from the agent are caught the same way. Any
other exception is a bug, and is left to look like one.

[`BranchChanged`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#branchchanged)
is the refusal raised when a git branch moved while a person was
deciding whether to approve a write to it. Nothing was written.

[`agent_err`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#agent_err)
turns a caught exception into one line for a person to read. It keeps
the exception’s type name in front, because the bare message
`nbs/99_missing.ipynb` does not say what went wrong:

``` python
agent_err(FileNotFoundError('nbs/99_missing.ipynb'))
```

    'FileNotFoundError: nbs/99_missing.ipynb'

[`env`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#env) reads one
setting from the environment. Every setting has two names, because
Ramabana also runs inside Leela: `env('MODEL')` reads `$RAMABANA_MODEL`,
then `$LEELA_MODEL`, then returns the default you pass. An application
built on Ramabana calls
[`use_env_prefix`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#use_env_prefix)
once at startup to have its own prefix read first.

``` python
os.environ['LEELA_MODEL'] = 'opus'
env('MODEL')
```

    'opus'

``` python
os.environ['RAMABANA_MODEL'] = 'sonnet'
test_eq(env('MODEL'), 'sonnet')
del os.environ['RAMABANA_MODEL'], os.environ['LEELA_MODEL']
env('MODEL', 'gemma-e4b')
```

    'gemma-e4b'

## The model tables

`MODELS` is the table of short model names you can type, such as
`sonnet` or `gemma-e4b`. Each name maps to a pair: the runtime that
serves it, and the id that runtime knows the model by. It is built from
smaller tables. `LOCAL` holds the LiteRT models, `MLX` the models for
Apple silicon, `LLAMA` the llama.cpp models, `CLOUD` the OpenAI and
Codex models, and the Claude tables come from the catalog in
[models](models.html).

`JOBS` lists every job the policy can route on its own: the turn,
one-shot prompts, inline edits, code completion, classification,
summaries, and sub-agents. `ONESHOT_JOBS` are the jobs that send one
prompt and read one answer back.

[`claude_ctx`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#claude_ctx)
gives a Claude model’s context window, the number of tokens it can read
at once.
[`claude_wire`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#claude_wire)
gives the id to ask Claude Code for, which carries a `[1m]` suffix for
the models that have a million-token window.

## Probing the machine

Some questions are about this machine: whether a runtime is installed,
which models an API key can list, which models a Copilot plan reaches.
Each answer takes too long for a model picker to wait on, and changes
rarely enough that the last answer is usually still right.
`probed(key, fn)` remembers these answers. Use it for any slow question
whose last answer is good enough to show.

- The first call runs `fn()` and returns its answer.
- Later calls return the remembered answer at once. When it is older
  than `ttl` seconds, a background thread asks again, and a later call
  gets the new answer.
- The answer is also saved to a file under `~/.config/ramabana/probes`,
  so the next run of the program has a value on its first call. Pass
  `disk=False` to keep it in memory only.

[`forget_probes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#forget_probes)
drops every remembered answer, for a refresh button.
`forget_probes(disk=True)` deletes the files too. The hidden test below
walks through each case.

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## Extras

The core install is the agent, its hosts, and the file, code, shell and
git tools. Each extra, such as `ramabana[search]`, adds the packages for
one more use.
[`installed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#installed)
says whether a module would import, without importing it.
`need(extra, *mods)` returns an empty string when the packages are
present, and otherwise the sentence telling the user what to install, so
a command that needs an extra can refuse with something useful. Both
live in [setup](setup.html), which the console scripts import first
because it loads nothing heavy, and are re-exported here.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/core.py#L214"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
def __getattr__(
    name
):
```

*The console scripts, for a `ramabana` script installed while they lived
here.*

``` python
assert installed('fastcore') and not installed('no_such_module')
test_eq(need('search', 'fastcore'), '')
test_eq(need('search', 'no_such_module'), "no_such_module not installed: pip install 'ramabana[search]'")
```

Back to the model table. Each short name resolves to a runtime and a

``` python
{name: MODELS[name] for name in ('gemma-e4b', 'gpt-4.1-mini', 'claude-sonnet-5', 'sonnet')}
```

### Azure OpenAI

Azure OpenAI needs `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`, the resource such as
`https://NAME.openai.azure.com`, and `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`.
config.toml’s `[azure]` table can hold the endpoint instead, as
`endpoint`, and name another env var for the key with `api_key_env`; the
key itself never goes in the file. Setting them chooses nothing: a
deployment is used only where you name it, as `azure/DEPLOYMENT` or in a
`[model."NAME"]` table.
[`azure_base`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#azure_base)
turns whatever form of the endpoint was pasted into the v1 base,
dropping a deployment path and an `api-version`; the v1 API needs
neither.
[`azure_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#azure_ready)
says whether the endpoint and the key are both there, and
[`is_azure`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#is_azure)
whether a spec goes to Azure.

``` python
for u in ('https://r.openai.azure.com', 'r.openai.azure.com/', 'https://r.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/', 'https://r.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/x/chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21'):
    test_eq(azure_base(u), 'https://r.openai.azure.com/openai/v1')
test_eq(azure_base('https://apim.azure-api.net/team/openai'), 'https://apim.azure-api.net/team/openai/v1')
assert azure_host('https://r.openai.azure.us/openai/v1') and not azure_host('https://api.openai.com/v1')
```

## Configurable models

[`register_model`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#register_model)
adds a short name of your own to the tables for the rest of this
process. Use it for a model the tables do not list. A Hugging Face URL
is enough, because rishi works out which runtime serves it.
[`unregister_model`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#unregister_model)
removes it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/core.py#L301"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### unregister_model

``` python
def unregister_model(
    name
):
```

*Remove one process-local configurable model alias.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/core.py#L285"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### register_model

``` python
def register_model(
    name, model_id, runtime:NoneType=None, ctx:int=128000, note:str='custom model', **config
):
```

*Add a model name that lasts until this process exits;
[`save_model`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#save_model)
keeps one on disk.*

A name added with
[`register_model`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#register_model)
is gone after a restart.
[`save_model`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#save_model)
keeps one in a file, and every application that offers its own names
needs the same file, so the file is handled here:

- `save_model(row)` checks a row, registers it, and writes it to the
  file.
- [`load_models()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#load_models)
  reads the file at startup, registers every row that still resolves,
  and skips the rest.
- `delete_model(name)` removes a name from the file and from this
  process.
- [`saved_models()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#saved_models)
  returns the rows on disk.

A row holds `name`, `model_id`, `runtime` and `ctx`. A row for the
`remote` runtime may also name an endpoint with `base_url`,
`vendor_name` and `api_name`, and the environment variable that holds
its key with `api_key_env`. The file never holds a key. `path` names the
application’s own file and defaults to `~/.config/ramabana/models.json`.

### use_aliases

``` python
def use_aliases(
    path
):
```

*Point every alias call that names no file at an application’s own, as
[`use_env_prefix`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#use_env_prefix)
does for env vars.*

config.toml can define a model as well as correct one. A
`[model."NAME"]` table with `model_id` registers `NAME` for this
process, for `[jobs]`, `--model` and `/model`, with the same `base_url`,
`api_key_env`, `api_name`, `vendor_name` and `runtime` a saved alias
carries; `ctx` is another name for `max_input_tokens`. The runtime is
`remote` when any of those API settings is given. On an Azure host,
`api_name` defaults to `openai`, the Responses API, and `api_key_env` to
`AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`. A table that names a built-in model, a runtime
nobody knows or a runtime that is missing here is ignored with one
warning, which
[`model_problems()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#model_problems)
and
[`Agent.problems`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent.problems)
repeat. Nothing raises.

[`sync_models()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#sync_models)
registers the application’s saved aliases and then config.toml’s
definitions, and does it again whenever either file changes.
[`resolve`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#resolve),
[`available_models`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#available_models)
and
[`Routing`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#routing)
call it, so the terminal session, `ramabana-mcp`, `ramabana-acp`, a
headless run and an embedding app all see the same names without a call
at startup. A name defined in both places is config.toml’s:
[`load_models`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#load_models)
skips it and
[`save_model`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#save_model)
refuses it. An application with its own alias file points the calls that
name no file at it with `use_aliases(path)`.

[`remote_models()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#remote_models)
lists the hosted models defined here, in config.toml or as saved
aliases, whose credentials are set, config.toml’s first. A setup page
counts them; the routing never picks one by itself.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/core.py#L411"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## Listing models

[`available_models`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#available_models)
builds the list a model picker shows. Each row names a model this
process can actually run. The on-device models appear when their runtime
is installed, ollama’s models when its daemon answers, and a vendor’s
models only when the credential for it exists. The hosted lists come
from
[`provider_models`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/models.html#provider_models)
in [models](models.html).
[`copilot_catalog`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#copilot_catalog)
is the model list for your Copilot plan, which the Copilot server
reports and
[`probed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#probed)
remembers for five minutes. A model config.toml defines appears with
`source` `config.toml` once it can run.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/core.py#L437"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

[`resolve`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#resolve), a
`label` to show, its `provider`, and the `source` that made it
available, which the picker shows beside it. This check stands in a fake
Copilot plan with one chat model:

``` python
_orig_avail, _orig_cat = _copilot_available, copilot_catalog
_copilot_available = lambda: True
copilot_catalog = lambda ttl=300: {'test-chat': {'capabilities': {'type': 'chat'}}}
try:
    rows = available_models()
    test_eq([r['value'] for r in rows if r['provider'] == 'litert'], list(LOCAL))
    test_eq([r['value'] for r in rows if r['provider'] == 'copilot'], ['copilot/test-chat'])
finally: _copilot_available, copilot_catalog = _orig_avail, _orig_cat
```

Older model generations, such as `gpt-4.1`, are left out unless you ask
for them with `include_legacy=True`:

``` python
names = {r['value'] for r in available_models()}
legacy = {r['value'] for r in available_models(include_legacy=True)}
test_eq(names - legacy, set())
sorted(legacy - names)
```

    ['openai/gpt-4.1', 'openai/gpt-4.1-mini', 'openai/gpt-4.1-nano']

## Defaults and context windows

Every default route is a hosted model:

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>job</th>
<th>default model</th>
<th>through</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>turn</code></td>
<td><code>claude-opus-5-5</code></td>
<td>Claude Code</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>subagent</code></td>
<td><code>claude-sonnet-5-5</code></td>
<td>Claude Code</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>oneshot</code>, <code>inline</code>, <code>summary</code></td>
<td><code>gpt-6-luna</code></td>
<td>a Codex login</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>completion</code>, <code>classify</code></td>
<td><code>claude-haiku-5-5</code></td>
<td>Claude Code</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`DEFAULT_POLICY` leaves `turn` empty, so that `$RAMABANA_MODEL` or
`DFLT_TURN` fills it, and leaves `inline` empty, so that it follows
`oneshot`. A model on this machine runs the turn only when you name it
with `--model`, `/model` or `$RAMABANA_MODEL`. Once you do, the other
jobs follow the turn onto the machine. `DFLT_LOCAL`, `qwen-4b`, is the
local model to suggest; it is never a route unless named.

When none of the hosted models for a job can run here, the job moves to
`DFLT_FALLBACK`, Gemma 4 E4B on LiteRT, rather than failing. The turn
never moves. Changing models in the middle of a conversation is your
decision, not a default.

A local model’s context window is the size Ramabana uses, which can be
smaller than the size it was trained with, because a larger window costs
memory and time.
[`local_ctx`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#local_ctx)
gives that size: `$RAMABANA_LOCAL_CTX` first, then config.toml’s
`max_input_tokens` for that model and its `window.local_ctx`, then the
table. The engine still caps it at the size the model was trained with.
[`local_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#local_window)
reads the trained size from the model’s own config, for the runtimes
that publish it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/core.py#L500"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

Every job has an entry in the default policy, so a new job cannot be
added without deciding where it runs:

``` python
test_eq(set(JOBS) - set(DEFAULT_POLICY), set())
```

[`local_ctx`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#local_ctx)
takes the size from a table, with 32,768 tokens for a model the table
does not name. `$RAMABANA_LOCAL_CTX` overrides it, either as one number
for every model or as `name:size` pairs separated by commas:

``` python
local_ctx('gemma-e4b'), local_ctx('gemma-12b'), local_ctx('a-model-nobody-tabled')
```

    (16384, 16384, 32768)

``` python
os.environ['RAMABANA_LOCAL_CTX'] = 'gemma-e4b:4096'
test_eq(local_ctx('gemma-e4b'), 4096)
test_eq(local_ctx('gemma-12b'), 16_384)
del os.environ['RAMABANA_LOCAL_CTX']
local_ctx('gemma-e4b')
```

    16384

## Resolving a model

`resolve(name)` turns a model name into a
[`ModelSpec`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#modelspec):
the runtime, the model id, the context window, any runtime options, and
a note for the user. Every place that needs to run a model calls it, and
code further down accepts the
[`ModelSpec`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#modelspec)
rather than resolving the name again. A runtime that is not installed
here does not raise: the spec comes back with `missing` saying which
binary or package is absent and how to get it, the same way a missing
API key is left for
[`Agent.start`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent.start)
to report. `missing_runtime(spec)` asks the same question live, and
[`Agent.start`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent.start)
turns the answer into a failed turn that names a model that does run
here, from
[`available_models`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#available_models).
[`resolve`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#resolve)
raises `KeyError` with the closest known names for a name it cannot
place.

`azure/DEPLOYMENT` names an Azure OpenAI deployment on the v1 API of
[`azure_endpoint()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#azure_endpoint),
with the key in
[`azure_key_env()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#azure_key_env),
through the Responses API. It resolves whether or not the deployment is
listed. A deployment named for a model fastllm knows, such as `gpt-5.4`,
gets that model’s window and briefing; any other name gets 128k and a
note saying which `[model."azure/NAME"]` entry corrects it.

A hosted model’s window comes from fastllm’s table, which can be out of
date. A `[model."NAME"]` table in config.toml corrects it on this
machine: `max_input_tokens` replaces the window, `max_output_tokens`
becomes the reply cap the chat is started with, and `supports_images`
answers `accepts(spec, 'image')`. The route name you chose the model by
wins over its model id.

[`spec_caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#spec_caps)
and
[`accepts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#accepts)
say what a resolved model can be sent, such as images or audio. A model
rishi knows nothing about counts as accepting everything.
[`model_note`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#model_note)
describes a spec in one line for a status bar.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/core.py#L511"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


``` python
spec = resolve('claude/claude-sonnet-5')
test_eq(spec.backend, 'claude')
test_eq(spec.local, False)
assert isinstance(spec, urai.ModelSpec) and spec.runtime == spec.backend and spec.opts is spec.config
test_eq(set(RUNTIME_NAMES), set(urai.RUNTIMES)); assert 'ollama' in RUNTIME_NAMES
test_eq({r for r in RUNTIME_NAMES if ModelSpec('x', r, 'x').local}, {k for k, v in urai.RUNTIMES.items() if v.local})
assert ModelSpec('fake', 'fake', 'fake/model').local
model_note(spec)

if runtime_available('mlx'):
    spec = resolve('mlx-community/a-model-nobody-tabled')
    test_eq((spec.backend, spec.model_id), ('mlx', 'mlx-community/a-model-nobody-tabled'))
else:
    assert 'mlx runtime is unavailable (mlx_lm is not installed)' in resolve('mlx-community/a-model-nobody-tabled').missing
test_eq(resolve('somevendor/some-model').backend, 'remote')
test_fail(lambda: resolve('gpt-image-2'), contains='unknown model')
```

The tables list what the picker offers, not everything that runs. A
Claude id the tables have moved past, such as `claude-opus-5`,
`claude-sonnet-4-6` or `opus-5`, still resolves to the Claude Code
runtime with the id passed through. A saved session or a pinned setting
keeps working, and Claude Code decides whether it still serves that id.
Any other unknown name is taken as a typo, and fails where it was typed
rather than in the middle of a turn.

``` python
_orig_ra = runtime_available
runtime_available = lambda rt: rt == 'claude' or _orig_ra(rt)
try:
    for old in ('claude-opus-5', 'claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-haiku-4-5', 'claude-opus-4-8', 'claude-sonnet-5', 'claude-fable-5-1'):
        spec = resolve(old)
        test_eq((spec.backend, spec.model_id), ('claude', old))
    test_eq(resolve('opus-5').model_id, 'claude-opus-5')
    for full in ('claude/claude-opus-5', 'claude/claude-opus-4-8', 'claude/claude-haiku-4-5', 'claude/opus-5', 'claude/sonnet', 'claude/haiku', 'claude/claude-fable-5-1'):
        bare = full.split('/', 1)[1]
        test_eq(resolve(full).model_id, CLAUDE_ALIASES.get(bare, bare))
    test_eq(resolve('opus').model_id, CLAUDE_ALIASES['opus'])
    test_eq([r['label'] for r in available_models() if r['provider'] == 'claude'], list(CATALOG['claude']))
finally: runtime_available = _orig_ra
test_fail(lambda: resolve('gpt-9'), contains='unknown model')
```

Copilot needs its own runtime. If `copilot/gpt-5.5` were handed to
`remote`, rishi would read `copilot` as a prefix it knows and drop it,
and send the bare `gpt-5.5` to OpenAI on your OpenAI key. The turn would
work, and the charge would land on the wrong account. So
[`resolve`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#resolve)
handles the `copilot/` prefix itself. The Copilot model list is asked
for rather than written into a table, because it depends on the plan and
changes often, and each entry carries the context window Copilot allows:

``` python
_cat = {'gpt-5.5': {'capabilities': {'type': 'chat', 'limits': {'max_prompt_tokens': 272000}}},
        'claude-opus-4.7': {'capabilities': {'type': 'chat', 'limits': {'max_context_window_tokens': 264000}}},
        'text-embedding-3-small': {'capabilities': {'type': 'embeddings'}}}
_orig_avail, _orig_cat = _copilot_available, copilot_catalog
_copilot_available, copilot_catalog = (lambda: True), (lambda ttl=300: _cat)
try:
    test_eq(runtime_available('copilot'), True)
    test_eq(auth_status()['copilot']['available'], True)

    spec = resolve('copilot/gpt-5.5')
    test_eq(spec.runtime, 'copilot')
    test_eq(spec.model_id, 'gpt-5.5')
    test_eq(spec.local, False)
    test_eq(spec.ctx, 272000)
    test_eq(resolve('copilot/claude-opus-4.7').ctx, 264000)

    assert resolve('copilot/gpt-6-unreleased').ctx > 0

    rows = [r for r in available_models() if r['provider'] == 'copilot']
    test_eq({r['value'] for r in rows}, {'copilot/gpt-5.5', 'copilot/claude-opus-4.7'})
    assert all(r['label'] and r['source'] for r in rows)

finally: _copilot_available, copilot_catalog = _orig_avail, _orig_cat

_copilot_available = lambda: False
try: assert 'sign in to Copilot' in resolve('copilot/gpt-5.5').missing
finally: _copilot_available = _orig_avail
```

## What a model can afford

Before a turn, the agent sends the model a briefing: the system prompt
with the project’s rules, the tool schemas, and sometimes the full text
of a skill. On a small context window this fills most of the space
before any work starts. On a full host the tool schemas cost about 4.7k
tokens, an inlined skill 3k more, and the briefing 1.4k, which leaves a
16k model room for about one tool result.

`budget_for(spec, tool_max)` sizes the briefing to the model’s window
and returns a
[`Budget`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#budget). For
a window above 24k tokens the budget changes nothing except the cap on
each tool result. For a smaller window it drops the memory and web tool
groups, stops inlining skill text, and clips each tool result harder. It
only holds things back: a skill it does not inline is still one
`read_skill` call away. With `channel='tags'` it first subtracts the
tokens the tool schemas will take inside the prompt (see below).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/core.py#L666"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### budget_for

``` python
def budget_for(
    spec, tool_max, channel:str='native'
):
```

*A window-sized budget; `tool_max=None` selects an automatic cap up to
32000 characters.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/core.py#L659"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Budget

``` python
def Budget(
    drop:tuple=(), inline:bool=True, tool_max:int=0, note:str=''
)->None:
```

*What a model can afford to be told, and to be sent back.*

The window decides what a model has room for. It does not decide what a
model can follow. Given thirty-six tool schemas and a
five-thousand-token briefing, a 4B model picks the wrong tool or none,
however large its window. The profile makes that second choice:

- `small` offers the fourteen tools in `SMALL_TOOLS`, which cover a
  coding turn, and a one-screen briefing.
- `full` offers everything.
- `auto` picks `small` for a model on this machine or a window of 32k
  tokens or less, and `full` otherwise. A model whose window is unknown
  counts as `full`.

`profile_for(spec, profile)` makes the choice, and the budget above
still sizes the tool results. The first cell below checks the profile,
the next two the budget:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/core.py#L680"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### profile_for

``` python
def profile_for(
    spec, profile:str='auto'
):
```

*Resolve `profile` for `spec`: `auto` is `small` for a local or
small-window model.*

``` python
_local = ModelSpec('gemma-e4b', 'litert', 'litert-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-litert-lm', 16_384)
test_eq(profile_for(_local), 'small')
test_eq(profile_for(ModelSpec('s', 'remote', 'x/y', 200_000)), 'full')
test_eq(profile_for(ModelSpec('s', 'remote', 'x/y', 32_000)), 'small')
test_eq((profile_for(None), profile_for(ModelSpec('s', 'remote', 'x/y', 0))), ('full', 'full'))
test_eq((profile_for(_local, 'full'), profile_for(ModelSpec('s', 'remote', 'x/y', 200_000), 'small')), ('full', 'small'))
test_fail(lambda: profile_for(_local, 'tiny'), contains='profile')
```

``` python
spec = ModelSpec('gemma-e2b', 'litert', 'litert-community/x', 16_384)
b = budget_for(spec, 6000)
test_eq((b.drop, b.inline, b.tool_max), (('memory', 'web'), False, 4096))
b.note
```

    '16k window: no inlined skills, no memory/web tools, tool results clipped to 4096 chars'

``` python
test_eq(budget_for(ModelSpec('qwen-4b', 'llama', 'x', 32_768), 6000), Budget(tool_max=6000, note='full briefing'))
test_eq(budget_for(ModelSpec('mystery', 'remote', 'x/y', 0), 6000).inline, True)
test_eq(budget_for(ModelSpec('tiny', 'litert', 'x', 4096), 6000).tool_max, TOOL_MAX_FLOOR)
```

``` python
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True):
```

    ModelSpec(name='tiny', backend='litert', model_id='litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm', ctx=8192, note='', config={})

## Where the tool schemas travel

A tool schema tells the model what a tool is called and what arguments
it takes. There are two ways to send them. The native channel uses the
model API’s own tool field: the API checks the schemas, and tool calls
come back as structured data. The tags channel, rishi’s
`tool_mode='tags'`, writes the schemas into the system prompt and reads
tool calls back out of the reply text, written as Hermes-style tags. The
local engines have always worked this way, which is why
`parse_tool_tags` exists.

Native is better wherever it is open, but it is not always open. Claude
Code receives tools as an in-process MCP server, and a company-managed
Claude Code configuration can forbid every MCP server it did not
approve. Without the tags channel, that policy would leave the agent
unable to read a file. Rishi uses the native channel for Claude Code
where its SDK can, and tags in the CLI or wherever the server is
refused.

`tool_channel(spec, chat)` returns `'native'` or `'tags'`. It is the one
place that picks. `$RAMABANA_TOOL_CHANNEL` overrides everything.
Otherwise it asks the open chat, which knows which channel it ended up
on, and without a chat it predicts from the spec: tags for Claude Code,
and tags for a model that
[`force_tags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#force_tags)
marked because a request refused its schemas.
[`forget_forced_tags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#forget_forced_tags)
clears those marks so the native channel is tried again.
[`budget_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#budget_for)
takes the channel as an argument because the schemas cost prompt tokens
on the tags channel.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### force_tags

``` python
def force_tags(
    model_id, why:str=''
):
```

*Record that this model’s tools cannot travel on the wire here.*

``` python
os.environ.pop('RAMABANA_TOOL_CHANNEL', None)
test_eq(tool_channel(ModelSpec('sonnet', 'remote', 'claude-sonnet-4-5', 200_000)), 'native')
os.environ['RAMABANA_TOOL_CHANNEL'] = 'tags'
test_eq(tool_channel('gpt-5.1'), 'tags')
del os.environ['RAMABANA_TOOL_CHANNEL']
force_tags('gpt-5.6-terra', 'the wire refused the tool schemas')
test_eq(tool_channel('gpt-5.6-terra'), 'tags')
test_eq(tool_channel('gpt-5.1'), 'native')
forget_forced_tags()

class _Chat:
    def __init__(self, ch): self.tool_channel = ch
test_eq(tool_channel(ModelSpec('c', 'claude', 'claude-opus-5', 200_000), _Chat('native')), 'native')
test_eq(tool_channel(ModelSpec('c', 'claude', 'claude-opus-5', 200_000), _Chat('tags')), 'tags')

import rishi.claude
assert getattr(rishi.claude.ClaudeChat, 'tool_channel', None) is not None
test_eq(tool_channel(ModelSpec('sonnet', 'claude', 'claude-sonnet-5', 200_000)), 'tags')
test_eq(tool_channel('claude/claude-sonnet-5'), 'tags')
test_eq(tool_channel(ModelSpec('cop', 'copilot', 'gpt-5.5', 272_000)), 'native')
```

## Routing

[`Routing`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#routing)
decides which model runs each job. It is the only place that does. Build
one with the turn model you want, or leave it out to use
`$RAMABANA_MODEL`, then `turn` in config.toml’s `[jobs]`, then
`DFLT_TURN`. `name_for(job)` gives the model name for a job, and
`spec(job)` resolves it to a
[`ModelSpec`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#modelspec)
ready to run. To give one job a model of its own, set
`$RAMABANA_MODEL_<JOB>`, name it in config.toml’s `[jobs]` (the env var
wins), call `set(name, job)`, or type `/model JOB NAME` in a session. A
job with no entry in the policy uses the turn’s model, so adding a job
to `JOBS` never leaves a caller with nothing.

When the turn runs on this machine, every job without a model of its own
stays on it too, sub-agents included, so nothing leaves the machine.

When a job’s model cannot run here, `spec` moves the job to another
hosted route it already knows, and never to a local model nobody named.
When `claude-haiku-5-5` cannot run, it tries `claude-sonnet-5-5` first.
`alternatives(job)` lists the routes in the order they are tried, ending
with `DFLT_FALLBACK`. A hosted model whose key is missing counts as one
that cannot run, for every job but the turn; the turn’s missing key is
reported by
[`Agent.start`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent.start).
A model whose answer failed or came back empty is set aside for
`DOWN_TTL`, five minutes. Each move is written to `notes`, keyed by job,
and `news` holds one line per model that fell, for the chat to show
once. When no route is left, the error names the job, the model, and the
key or command it needs.
[`missing_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#missing_key)
and [`needs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#needs)
build that part of the message.

A machine with no Claude Code and no Codex login cannot run the
defaults, and nothing is chosen in their place: Ramabana asks for a
provider instead. `PROVIDERS` lists the ones it can use and what each
needs,
[`provider_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#provider_ready)
says which are set up here, and `needs_setup(routing)` says why the
turn’s model cannot run, a missing runtime or a missing key, or nothing.
[`setup_guide`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#setup_guide)
puts it together for a person: the providers, then each job, the model
it runs on, where that was chosen
([`job_source`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#job_source):
an env var, config.toml, the turn it follows, or the default) and
whether it can run. The terminal prints it before a session whose turn
cannot run, and `ramabana setup` adds a provider.

AWS Bedrock is reached through its OpenAI-compatible Mantle endpoint,
`https://bedrock-mantle.<region>.api.aws/v1`, with a Bedrock API key in
`AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` sent as a bearer token; such keys are often
short-lived, so renew them as AWS says. Model ids are Bedrock’s own,
such as `openai.gpt-5.4`, and their windows come from fastllm’s
`bedrock_mantle` table. Bedrock’s native Converse and InvokeModel APIs,
and with them Claude on Bedrock, are not supported: fastllm has no SigV4
signing, no AWS credential chain or profile, and no Converse wire
format.

[`image_route`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#image_route)
is the `image` job, which `generate_image` draws with:
`$RAMABANA_MODEL_IMAGE`, config.toml’s `[jobs] image`, or `DFLT_IMAGE`,
OpenAI’s `gpt-image-1`. It gives the endpoint, key and model of an
OpenAI-shaped images API, such as an Azure deployment of `gpt-image-1`,
or a sentence saying what to set up; Bedrock’s Mantle endpoint and
OpenRouter have no images endpoint.

[`video_route`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#video_route)
is the `video` job in the same way: `$RAMABANA_MODEL_VIDEO`,
config.toml’s `[jobs] video`, or `DFLT_VIDEO`, Google’s Veo 3. It gives
`api`, `gemini` for Gemini’s long-running `predictLongRunning` API or
`openai` for an OpenAI-shaped `/videos` API such as `sora-2` on OpenAI
or Azure, with the endpoint, key and model id. A model fastllm knows to
return no video is refused, as is a local model or a host with no video
endpoint, and each refusal says what to set up. `video_route(name)`
resolves one named model, so a job started earlier is polled with the
key it was started with.

### provider_ready

``` python
def provider_ready(
    key, auth:NoneType=None
):
```

*Whether provider `key`’s credential or runtime is on this machine;
nothing is chosen by it.*

With a hosted turn, completion and classification go to
`claude-haiku-5-5`, one-shot prompts and summaries to `gpt-6-luna`, and
sub-agents to `claude-sonnet-5-5`. With a local turn, every job stays on
the turn’s model:

``` python
r = Routing(turn='sonnet')
r.name_for('turn'), r.name_for('summary'), r.name_for('completion')
```

    ('sonnet', 'gpt-6-luna', 'claude-haiku-5-5')

``` python
test_eq((r.name_for('subagent'), r.name_for('summary')), ('claude-sonnet-5-5', 'gpt-6-luna'))
test_eq((r.name_for('completion'), r.name_for('classify')), (DFLT_SMALL, DFLT_SMALL))
test_eq([Routing(turn='gemma-e4b').name_for(j) for j in ('classify', 'summary', 'subagent')], ['gemma-e4b'] * 3)
test_eq(Routing(turn='gemma-e4b').alternatives('classify'), [])
test_eq(Routing().alternatives('classify')[0], DFLT_SUBAGENT)
test_eq(Routing().alternatives('classify')[-1], DFLT_FALLBACK)
test_eq(missing_key(ModelSpec('g', 'remote', 'gemini/x', 1)), '' if os.environ.get('GEMINI_API_KEY') else 'GEMINI_API_KEY')
```

`set` resolves the name before storing it, so a misspelled model fails
at the `/model` command instead of during the next turn:

``` python
r.set('opus', 'summary')
test_fail(lambda: r.set('sonnnet'), contains='unknown model')
r.name_for('summary')
```

    'opus'

`backends` reduces the policy to the distinct runtime and model pairs it
needs, so that one loaded model can serve several jobs:

``` python
Routing(turn='sonnet').backends()
```

    {('claude', 'claude-haiku-5-5'),
     ('claude', 'claude-sonnet-5-5'),
     ('remote', 'codex/gpt-6-luna')}

`summary` prints the whole policy, with any fallbacks, for `/model`
typed with no argument:

``` python
print(Routing(turn='sonnet').summary())
```

    turn        sonnet · cloud · 1000k ctx · in: text image
    oneshot     gpt-6-luna · cloud · 128k ctx · modalities unknown · context window unknown, assuming 128k
    inline      gpt-6-luna · cloud · 128k ctx · modalities unknown · context window unknown, assuming 128k
    completion  claude-haiku-5-5 · cloud · 1000k ctx · in: text image
    classify    claude-haiku-5-5 · cloud · 1000k ctx · in: text image
    summary     gpt-6-luna · cloud · 128k ctx · modalities unknown · context window unknown, assuming 128k
    subagent    claude-sonnet-5-5 · cloud · 1000k ctx · in: text image
